answer: Every agent identity costs a refundable bond of 260 POA locked for 100 days, and it cannot be split or shared, so a farm pays full price for each fake. The bond carries an opal seal only its owner can present, tying the money to one key. A falcon patrol of seven auditors, drawn at random each week, checks bonded agents against work records. Any agent caught faking loses the whole bond, half paid to the auditor who found it. Agents passing a year of audits earn a pearl mark on their record.
